newsitem.title: USA: Oxford to offer alternative medicine plan.
newsitem.headline: Oxford to offer alternative medicine plan.

text.p: Oxford Health Plans Inc on Tuesday said that starting at the beginning of next year a plan will be available to its members covering visits to chiropractors, acupuncturists and yoga instructors.
The Norwalk, Conn.-based health maintenance organization is the first major U.S. health plan to try to tap into the estimated $50 billion-a-year U.S. alternative healthcare market.

A key catalyst for the company launching the service was a Oxford Health survey showing that a third of the company's 1.4 million members said they had used alternative health care in the past 12 months, senior vice president David Snow said.

"This is not fad stuff we're talking about," Snow said in an interview during the plan's unveiling in Central Park. "These are disciplines that have been around for 5,000 years. There's some substance to it."
It said Oxford's commercial payors, such as employers, can add the alternative coverage to their plans by paying an extra three percent over the cost of their current contract.
The plan will be offered in Connecticut, New York and New Jersey, covering visits to chiropractors, massage therapists, clinical nutritionists and registered dietitians.
Visits to naturopathic physicians will only be covered in Connecticut pending their licensing in New York and New Jersey, the company said.
It said it expected to have between 500 and 1,000 holistic health providers signed up for its alternative medicine program by January 1.

Supplies of echinacea, valeriana, slippery elm throat lozenges and other alternative medicines will not be covered but will be offered at discount prices through an Oxford mail-order system, executives said.

Oxford chief executive Stephen Wiggins told a news conference that the company was not trying to supplant traditional medicine in its coverage, but saw the alternative medicine as an addition to traditional medical care.
"This is not ... a replacement for Western medical services," Wiggins said.

The company will be compiling a database to help determine who purchases the alternative medical benefits, trends in its utilization and whether it improves the health of those using it and increases or decreases overall medical costs.
Oxford's stock was unchanged at 48 in afternoon trading.
